title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Lewis University spaces for studying, getting feedback, meeting classmates, exercising, viewing art, reflecting, and building projects.

cards.title: Reserve the Room Before the Group Chat Spirals
cards.subtitle: Bookable study space inside the Learning Resource Center
cards.notes: Use the library’s reservation link before a group session, then bring assignment files and confirm current building hours online.
cards.short_summary: A practical base for focused work, research help, and scheduled group study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lewis University Library provides a Reserve a Study Space service, research assistance, and regular semester hours.
cards.access_notes: Check the library page for current semester or summer hours and use its reservation service for bookable spaces.

cards.title: Bring the Rubric, Not Just the Draft
cards.subtitle: First-floor peer-writing support in the LRC
cards.notes: Schedule a 30-, 60-, or 90-minute visit and arrive with the prompt, rubric, draft, and specific questions for the writing mentor.
cards.short_summary: A named campus workspace where writers can talk through revisions with a mentor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Writing Center offers in-person appointments with mentors on the first floor of the Learning Resource Center for writers at any stage.
cards.access_notes: Appointments must be scheduled through the Writing Center; in-person, phone, and video formats are offered.

cards.entity_name: Brother James Gaffney, FSC Student Center
cards.title: Start Where Student Groups Actually Work
cards.subtitle: Student Engagement, Student Senate, dining, and Common Grounds under one roof
cards.notes: Use the lower level when coordinating an organization or Student Senate question, then choose an agreed meeting point inside the center.
cards.short_summary: A multi-use student hub that combines involvement offices, gathering space, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The current campus map places Student Engagement, Multicultural Student Enrichment, Student Senate, and Common Grounds on the center’s lower level, with Brown Dining Hall upstairs.
cards.access_notes: Campus access and individual office or dining availability may vary; consult the relevant Lewis office before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Café as a Precise Meetup Point
cards.subtitle: Named dining stop on the student center’s lower level
cards.notes: Name Common Grounds—not just “the student center”—when meeting classmates, and check dining availability before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A clearly identified campus café that makes an easy-to-describe rendezvous point.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University’s current campus map identifies Common Grounds as a dining location on the lower level of the Brother James Gaffney, FSC Student Center.
cards.access_notes: Dining availability is not stated on the campus-map page; verify current service information before relying on it.

cards.entity_name: JFK Student Recreation and Sports Center
cards.title: Reserve a Court Instead of Hoping One Is Open
cards.subtitle: Courts, equipment, programs, fitness facilities, and a pool
cards.notes: Check the facility schedule first; eligible members can reserve a court up to 48 hours ahead and ask about available sports equipment.
cards.short_summary: The campus recreation complex supports planned workouts and shared games beyond varsity athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: The center provides fitness, wellness, intramural, and recreational programs, along with equipment service and court reservations up to 48 hours in advance.
cards.access_notes: Membership rules apply. The official page currently lists summer hours and directs users to the facility schedule for updates.

cards.title: Take the Conversation onto the Marked Trail
cards.subtitle: A dawn-to-dusk campus route through native Illinois plantings
cards.notes: Go with another person during daylight, remain on the marked trail, and skip the walk when lightning, ice, heavy snow, or high winds threaten.
cards.short_summary: A campus walking and running route suited to a daylight reset with a classmate.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis says students, faculty, and staff can walk or run on the trail, which contains native species and is open from dawn to dusk with users asked to stay on the route.
cards.source_title: Sustainability Areas — Burnham Centennial Nature Trail
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk. Stay on the trail, visit with another person, and avoid hazardous weather conditions.

cards.entity_name: Brent and Jean Wadsworth Family Gallery
cards.title: Let the Current Exhibit Set the Discussion Topic
cards.subtitle: Original art by visiting artists and members of the Lewis community
cards.notes: Check the exhibition schedule, meet inside Oremus Fine Arts Center, and leave time to compare one work each before discussing the show.
cards.short_summary: A rotating exhibition space that gives classmates something concrete to examine together.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery presents original work by local, regional, national, and international artists, including the Lewis community, and opens daily during scheduled exhibitions.
cards.source_title: The Brent and Jean Wadsworth Family Gallery
cards.access_notes: Open daily 9:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. during scheduled exhibits; closed for holiday breaks, with closures posted on gallery social channels.

cards.title: Choose a Room That Matches the Conversation
cards.subtitle: Lounges, meeting rooms, ministry offices, a pantry, and a meditation garden
cards.notes: Ask Mission and Ministry which room fits your purpose, whether you need a lounge conversation, pantry assistance, or quieter reflection.
cards.short_summary: A collection of named support, gathering, and reflection spaces beside the chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The LaGrippe Pastoral Center includes the D’Arcy Great Room, Lewis Family Room, Living Room student lounge, Food Pantry, meditation room, garden, and staff offices.
cards.access_notes: Contact University Mission and Ministry for room availability, pantry procedures, programs, or visitor access.

cards.title: Step Away Without Leaving Campus
cards.subtitle: A designated reflection room in the LaGrippe Pastoral Center
cards.notes: Use the room for quiet prayer or reflection, keep conversation low, and check with Mission and Ministry if a group needs coordinated access.
cards.short_summary: A specifically designated campus room for contemplative pauses across faith traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Lewis University identifies the Multifaith Prayer and Meditation Room as a feature of the James A. LaGrippe Pastoral Center and marks it as a worship or prayer location.
cards.access_notes: Use respectfully as a prayer and meditation space; contact Mission and Ministry for current access guidance.

cards.title: Give the Project a Real Workbench
cards.subtitle: Collaborative workspaces, lounge access, a maker lab, and mentorship
cards.notes: Review the student membership option, apply before depending on access, and identify whether your team needs the lounge, maker lab, or mentorship.
cards.short_summary: A north-campus workspace for students developing entrepreneurial and creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Innovation Hub offers students a membership path with lounge and maker-lab access and describes collaborative workspaces for focused and team work.
cards.access_notes: Located in SB-122 at 101 W. Airport Road. Access requires an application and completed membership onboarding.
